### HS-51 — THE NEW HAND AMONG OLD LINES (the relief's hand)
When the inciting fact is a new handwriting in an old book (CHAIN-73's fifth hand at 03:00), frame 0 must show the new line WITH its neighbors — the fourth hand's lines above and below it — the viewer reads a stranger, not an error. Restage rule: the new line must be shot in a run of old lines (three lines minimum in frame: old, new, old) — a lone new line is a typo; a new line among old lines is a person. Companion to HS-48 (the blank line as a name): HS-48 makes a blank a person; HS-51 makes a handwriting a person — one names by absence, the other names by difference. Sources: lighthouse keepers' relief — the relief's hand in the log was how the station knew the watch had changed (wikipedia.org "Lighthouse keeper").

### HS-52 — THE MISMATCHED SIGNATURE (two hands, one guest)
When the inciting fact is an arrival that does not match its promise (CHAIN-74's arrival hand vs yesterday's pre-signature), frame 0 must hold BOTH signatures legible in ONE spread — the pre-signature above, the arrival below, same light, same book — the viewer reads two hands, not one sloppy hand. Restage rule: shoot the book SPREAD, never two separate frames — separate frames make it a correction, one spread makes it a question; the date on each line must read (yesterday above, today below) so the mismatch is dated, not merely drawn. Companion to HS-50 (the date before the name): HS-50 makes the date a verb; HS-52 makes the mismatch a person — one dates the claim, the other doubts it. Sources: hotel registers at check-in — the house compared the arrival signature against the reservation, and a mismatch meant a second person, not a bad pen (wikipedia.org "Guest book").

### LORE-26 — THE FIFTH HAND (recurring cast backstory as serial setting)
CHAIN-73 introduces the network's fifteenth rule-person: the station's RELIEF — a fifth hand that signs logs but never books, tends the owed lamp but never the desk lamp, covers the round but never keeps the chair. Backstory: the founder's relief rule — "a station keeps its hours by its reliefs, not its regulars" — and the relief is hired for the owed duty only, never for the round (Chain AO: the lighthouse relief — the relief keeper worked the double watch, never the station). Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the relief's hand is the station's clock for absence — a fifth-hand line means the fourth hand is away, and the log's "RELIEF." ruling is the station admitting it (CHAIN-73 P3's line: "Relief covers the owed."). Rule — the relief law: the fifth hand is shown only as a LINE (in the log) and a STATE (a tended lamp), never as a figure on camera — a relief seen is a character introduced, and the relief is a function, not a cast member (CRAFT-235 extends: a tending staged is a tending collapsed; a relief staged is a relief spent). Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25): set in CHAIN-73; the fifth hand never tends the desk lamp before CHAIN-76, and the fifth hand's name is never written — like the fourth hand, the relief marks, never names.

### CLIFF-MECH-25 — THE RELIEF
The withheld fact is a PERSON by a SUBSTITUTION — the cliff frame shows a duty DONE in a new hand (CHAIN-73 P1's fifth-hand 03:00 line, lamp tended), never the worker who did it. Rule: the new hand must be SHOWN beside the old hand before it is doubted — old, new, old in one frame (HS-51): an unshown new hand is a riddle, a shown new hand among old lines is a stranger. The next part spends it by RULING the cover (CHAIN-73 P3's margin ruling: "RELIEF.") — the spend is a ruling, not a reveal: the station names the function, never the person. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-22 (the second signature): the second signature withholds a PERSON by a hand; the relief withholds a person by a COVER — one marks paper, the other marks work. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-24 (the contradicting clock): the contradicting clock withholds a TIME by two states; the relief withholds a WORKER by a done duty — one marks an hour, the other marks a hand. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: lighthouse keeper relief — the relief's line in the log was the watch changing hands, and the station ruled the change, never introduced the relief (wikipedia.org "Lighthouse keeper").

- **CRAFT-241 — THE NEW HAND NEEDS ITS NEIGHBORS.** CHAIN-73 teaches that a new handwriting is only legible against old handwriting: frame the new line with its neighbors, or the viewer reads a typo. Rule: a draft whose hook is a new hand must name the old hands it sits among (whose lines above and below) — an unneighbored new hand is set dressing; a neighbored new hand is a stranger. Prepro test: cover the neighboring lines in the premise's frame 0 — if the hook survives, the neighbors weren't carrying it, and the draft hasn't found its stranger yet. Sources: lighthouse keepers' relief — the relief's hand was read against the keeper's hand, and the difference was the news.
- **CRAFT-242 — THE ARRIVAL MUST NOT MATCH.** CHAIN-74 teaches that when an arrival hand differs from its promise, the difference IS the plot — and a draft that "fixes" the mismatch kills the chain. Rule: a draft with two signatures for one guest must keep both hands distinct (different pressure, different shape, different date) and must never reconcile them in the premise — reconciliation is the next chain's spend, not this chain's premise. Prepro audit: if the premise's P1 frame shows only one signature, the mismatch isn't built yet; if it shows two matching signatures, the chain is already spent. Sources: hotel registers — the house kept the mismatch, and the mismatch kept the guest honest.
- **CRAFT-243 — THE TURNED CHAIR IS A PROMOTION.** CHAIN-75 teaches that a chair's facing is its job description, and turning a chair reassigns its worker: XIV facing the lamp is a tender's chair, XIV facing the arc is a sitter's chair — the turn, not the sitting, is the promotion. Rule: a draft that moves a chair must name the facing in the rota line (facing what, since when) — an unnoted facing is furniture moved; a noted facing is a worker reassigned. Prepro test: read the premise's rota line — if it lists chairs without facings, the premise has miscounted its workforce's jobs. Sources: the Speaker's chair — the chair's facing was the office, and sitting in it was taking the office, not taking a seat.

Restage rule: shoot the SPREAD with both names legible and yesterday's nameless pre-signature visible above — a lone named line is a guest; a named line below a guest's line, in yesterday's nameless hand, is a proxy become visitor. Companion to HS-51 (the new hand among old lines): HS-51 makes a handwriting a person; HS-54 makes a naming a visitor — one introduces by difference, the other promotes by name. Sources: letters of introduction — the voucher's name, once written, made the voucher answerable, and the letter itself was "a draft for payment on demand" (Etiquette ch. XXVIII; wikipedia.org "Letter of introduction").

### LORE-27 — THE PROXY'S PRICE (recurring cast backstory as serial setting)
CHAIN-77 introduces the network's vouching rule: a promise buys TWO chairs — the guest's and the proxy's. Backstory: the founder's vouching rule — "a station that accepts a vouching accepts the voucher" — and the proxy's name, once written, makes the proxy a visitor with a chair (chair XII, one before the guest's XIII, seated voucher-before-guest). Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the proxy's price is the promise itself — CHAIN-77 P3's line: "Promise spent, both seated." Rule — the vouching law: a proxy is shown only as a HAND until named, and once named, the proxy is seated, never merely listed — a named proxy unseated is a promise unspent. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26): set in CHAIN-77; the proxy never vouches a second guest before CHAIN-80, and the proxy's chair (XII) is never re-plated before the guest's hour ends.

### CLIFF-MECH-26 — THE CALLED HOUR
The withheld fact is a WORD by a RULING — the cliff frame shows a word SPOKEN (CHAIN-76 P1's "Three.") without saying whether the word is speech or an hour-call. Rule: the word must be SHOWN as spoken before it is ruled — a ruled word never heard is a memo; a heard word awaiting its ruling is an hour. The next part spends it by RULING the word (CHAIN-76 P3's margin ruling: "HOUR CALLED.") — the spend is a ruling, not a transcript: the station names the function, never quotes the speech. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-25 (the relief): the relief withholds a person by a cover; the called hour withholds a word by a ruling — one marks work, the other marks speech. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-22 (the second signature): the second signature withholds a person by a hand; the called hour withholds a word by a ruling — one marks paper, the other marks speech. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: town criers — the cry was a summons plus an hour, ruled by the town as the hour's call, and "o'clock" itself is the cry's fossil (turnerpublishing.net town-crier piece).

- **CRAFT-244 — THE FIRST WORD MUST BE SHORT.** CHAIN-76 teaches that a first word longer than one beat is a speech, and a speech ends the silence the series built. Rule: a draft giving a silent worker their first word must keep it to one word, and the word must be a time, a name, or a number — never an opinion. Prepro test: count the first word's beats — if it takes more than one beat to say, the worker has given a speech, not a word. Sources: town criers — "Oyez" was one word, and the hour followed.
- **CRAFT-245 — COVERAGE CREEP IS A PROMOTION.** CHAIN-78 teaches that a relief who covers a second duty has been promoted by coverage — the scope grew without a ruling. Rule: a draft that widens a relief's cover must name the widening in the rota line (covering what, since when) — an unnoted widening is scope drift; a noted widening is a promotion. Prepro test: read the rota line — if the relief covers more than the premise's first duty, the premise has promoted its relief. Sources: lighthouse relief — the relief who worked the double watch owned the watch, not just the night.
- **CRAFT-246 — A DATED ABSENCE IS A PROMISE.** CHAIN-78 teaches that dating a departure without a destination is not withholding — it is promising a return on a date the station will have to keep. Rule: a draft that dates an absence must also date the relief's end (the leave line's pair) — a lone dated absence is a disappearance; a paired dated absence is a rotation. Prepro test: find the absence's pair date — if the premise dates a leave without dating the cover's end, the rotation isn't built yet. Sources: lighthouse keeper leave — the log dated the departure, and the relief's term dated the return.

### HS-55 — THE SECONDED WORD (the tender's second word)
When the inciting fact is a second word (CHAIN-79's tender mid-second-word), frame 0 must show the mouth OPEN mid-word WITH the first word already logged on the program sheet in the same frame — a lone open mouth is a first word; an open mouth beside a logged first word is a seconding. ### LORE-28 — THE OVERLAP (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-81 introduces the founder's handover law: "no lamp is left between hands." Backstory: the fourth hand was once a relief themselves — they covered a watch whose keeper never returned, and one night the lamp went untended between the relief's end and the next hand's beginning; the founder wrote the overlap law that night, and the station has overlapped every handover since. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the overlap is the fourth hand's own history — CHAIN-81 P3's line: "No lamp between hands." Rule — the overlap law: a returning hand and a relief must share one frame on the lamp before the relief's leave is honored — a return with no overlap is a date, not a handover. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26/LORE-27): set in CHAIN-81; the fifth hand's next watch is never named before CHAIN-84, and the overlap frame (two hands, one lamp) is never reused before the relief's departure airs.

### CLIFF-MECH-27 — THE OVERLAP
The withheld fact is a WATCH by a HANDOVER — the cliff frame shows two hands on one lamp (CHAIN-81 P1) without saying whose watch the lamp is on. Rule: both hands must be SHOWN holding before the watch is named — a named watch never held is a memo; a held lamp awaiting its watch is a handover. The next part spends it by RULING the watch (CHAIN-81 P3's margin ruling: "OVERLAP KEPT.") — the spend is a ruling that the lamp belonged to the handover, not to either hand. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-25 (the relief): the relief withholds a person by a cover; the overlap withholds a watch by a handover — one marks work, the other marks the exchange. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-26 (the called hour): the called hour withholds a word by a ruling; the overlap withholds a watch by a handover — one marks speech, the other marks duty. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: guard mounting — old and new guard form up facing each other and a key is handed over, symbolizing the exchange of responsibilities (wikipedia.org "Guard mounting").

- **CRAFT-247 — A SECOND WORD MUST SECOND, NOT REPEAT.** CHAIN-79 teaches that a second word that merely repeats the first is an echo, and an echo ends the hour's argument. Rule: a draft giving a worker a second word must make the second word do new procedural work — second, qualify, or spend the first — never restate it. Prepro test: cover the first word — if the second word still means something alone, it is a new speech, not a seconding; if it means nothing alone, it seconds. - **CRAFT-248 — A SECOND VOUCHING DOUBLES THE PROMISE, NOT THE GUEST.** CHAIN-80 teaches that a voucher's second vouching adds a backer, not a party — the guest count is not the promise's strength. Rule: a draft adding a second vouching must show the first promise STRENGTHENED (confirmed, backed, witnessed) — a second vouching that merely adds chairs is a guest list, not a confirmation. Prepro test: remove the second guest — if the first guest's seat weakens, the vouching confirmed; if nothing changes, it only listed. Sources: confirmed letter of credit — the confirming bank pays even if the issuing bank fails; two promises, one payment.
- **CRAFT-249 — A RETURN MUST OVERLAP, NOT REPLACE.** CHAIN-81 teaches that a clean swap with no shared frame is a disappearance with a date, not a return. Rule: a draft returning a hand must stage one frame where both hands hold the duty at once — the overlap frame — before the outgoing hand's leave is honored. Prepro test: find the overlap frame — if the outgoing hand's last frame and the returning hand's first frame share no duty, the return hasn't been staged yet. Sources: guard mounting — the key is handed over between guards formed up facing each other; the handover, not the date, transfers responsibility.

### HS-57 — THE TWICE-LOGGED WORD (the tender's third word)
When the inciting fact is a third word (CHAIN-82's tender mid-third-word), frame 0 must show the mouth OPEN mid-word WITH the first two words already logged on the program sheet in the same frame — a lone open mouth is a first word; an open mouth beside one logged word is a seconding; an open mouth beside TWO logged words is a reading. Restage rule: shoot the sheet's two logged lines ("THREE — CALLED.", "SECONDED BY THE HOUR.") legible beside the chair — if either logged word isn't in frame, the third word reads as a first. Companion to HS-55 (the seconded word): HS-55 makes a second open mouth a seconding; HS-57 makes a third open mouth a reading — one weighs a word, the other reads a text. ### HS-58 — THE WITNESSING HAND (the proxy witnessing the third vouching)
When the inciting fact is a witnessed vouching (CHAIN-83's third guest), frame 0 must show the proxy's HAND resting BESIDE the second guest's vouching line — not on it, not over it, not signing it. Restage rule: shoot the witness hand BESIDE the line with the vouching hand's signature visible between them — a hand ON the line is a second voucher; a hand OVER the line is a correction; a hand BESIDE the line is a witness. Companion to HS-56 (the confirming hand): HS-56 makes a resting hand a confirmation; HS-58 makes a beside hand a witness — one backs by touch, the other proves by presence. ### LORE-29 — THE UNPLATED CHAIR (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-84 introduces the founder's relief law: "a relief's chair is never plated." Backstory: the founder once plated a relief's chair after a long cover, and the relief never returned — the chair had become a keeper's, and there was no relief's chair left to come back to; since then relief chairs stay unplated, so a relief can always return to the station they covered. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the unplated chair is the fifth hand's return ticket — CHAIN-84 P3's line: "Chair unplated, return open." Rule — the unplated-chair law: a relief's chair is shown empty and unplated after departure, never re-plated, never sat by a keeper — a plated relief chair is a relief retired. ### CLIFF-MECH-28 — THE THIRD READING
The withheld fact is a WORD by a READING — the cliff frame shows a third word SPOKEN (CHAIN-82 P1's "Read.") without saying whether it reads the hour's log or moves a new hour. Rule: the first two words must be SHOWN logged before the third is read — a reading of nothing logged is a speech; a logged text awaiting its reading is a third word. The next part spends it by RULING the text (CHAIN-82 P3's margin ruling: "READ BY THE LOG.") — the spend is a ruling that names the text, not a transcript: the station names what was read, never quotes the reading. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-26 (the called hour): the called hour withholds a word by a ruling; the third reading withholds a word by a text — one marks speech, the other marks the record. - **CRAFT-252 — A DEPARTURE MUST LEAVE A LAMP, NOT A VACANCY.** CHAIN-84 teaches that a departure honored over an uncovered lamp is an abandonment, not a transfer. ### LORE-30 — THE WAITING LAMP (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-87 introduces the founder's waiting law: "no lamp waits dark for a named keeper." Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the waiting lamp is the fifth hand's welcome — CHAIN-87 P3's line: "Arrived to light." Rule — the waiting-lamp law: a lamp awaiting a named keeper is shown lit with its log line "AWAITED — NAMED." every night of the wait, never dark, never gap-logged — a dark waiting lamp is a station that failed its own law. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26/LORE-27/LORE-28/LORE-29): set in CHAIN-87; the fifth hand's first watch at the receiving station never airs before CHAIN-88, and the receiving station's log-keeper is never named before the fifth hand's arrival airs.

### HS-61 — THE ALONE WATCH (the fifth hand's first watch alone)
When the inciting fact is a lone watch (CHAIN-88's fifth hand alone at the receiving lamp), frame 0 must show ONE hand on the lamp WITH the other chairs EMPTY in the same frame — a lone hand with no chairs is a keeper; a lone hand beside empty chairs is a watch kept alone. Restage rule: shoot the empty chairs legible beside the lamp — if the chairs aren't in frame, the aloneness reads as an empty station. Companion to HS-60 (the waiting lamp): HS-60 makes a lit lamp with a named wait a watch; HS-61 makes a lone hand with empty chairs a watch kept — one awaits a keeper, the other keeps alone. Sources: a lighthouse keeper's first night — the keeper's log is the only witness of a lone watch (wikipedia.org "Lighthouse keeper").

### HS-62 — THE FIFTH LINE (the fifth guest's sealed vouching)
When the inciting fact is a sealed vouching (CHAIN-89's fifth guest), frame 0 must show FIVE lines down the page WITH the book's seal pressed across the chain's foot in the same frame — five lines with no seal is a longer list; five lines under a seal is a chain closed. Restage rule: shoot the seal legible across the chain's foot — if the seal isn't in frame, the fifth line reads as an uncounted guest. Companion to HS-58 (the witnessing hand): HS-58 makes a beside hand a witness; HS-62 makes a seal across the chain a close — one proves by presence, the other closes by seal. Sources: a web of trust — beyond counting depth, the seal carries the trust, not the links (wikipedia.org "Web of trust").

### LORE-31 — THE COUNTING LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-89 introduces the founder's counting law: "the station counts to four." Backstory: the founder once counted a chain of seven guests link by link and lost the middle link — the chain stood, but no one could say which guest had vouched for whom, and the hour sat seven strangers; since then chains are counted to four links, and any link beyond the fourth is sealed by the book, not counted — the seal closes what the count cannot hold. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the counting law is the fifth guest's admission — CHAIN-89 P3's line: "Sealed, standing." Rule — the counting law: a vouching chain is shown counted link by link to four, and any fifth link is shown under the book's seal, never counted as a fifth link — a counted fifth link is a chain miscounted. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26/LORE-27/LORE-28/LORE-29/LORE-30): set in CHAIN-89; the sixth vouching never airs before CHAIN-91, and the book's seal is never shown pressed before the fifth guest's line is written.

### CLIFF-MECH-30 — THE FIRST WORD
The withheld fact is a WORD by a RETURN — the cliff frame shows a tender's mouth OPEN after silence (CHAIN-90 P1's "Heard again.") with the log line "SPOKEN — ?" beside them, without saying whether the word greets the hour or moves a motion. Rule: the silence must be SHOWN ended before the word is ruled — an unended silence makes the word a fifth word; a silence ended by a greeting makes it a first. The next part spends it by RULING the word (CHAIN-90 P3's margin ruling: "FIRST WORD GREETED, COUNTED FIRST.") — the spend is a ruling that counts the word, not a transcript: the station names what the word did, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-29 (the silence): the silence withholds a word by a seat; the first word withholds a word by a return — one marks presence, the other marks greeting. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-28 (the third reading): the third reading withholds a word by a text; the first word withholds a word by a return — one marks the record, the other marks the greeting. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: the talkies' first line — it greets the audience before it moves any plot (wikipedia.org "The Jazz Singer").

- **CRAFT-256 — A FIRST WATCH MUST BE ALONE, NOT EMPTY.** CHAIN-88 teaches that a receiving station shown with no keeper is an empty station, and an empty station ends the transfer's argument. Rule: a draft staging a first watch alone must show the keeper's hand on the lamp AND the empty chairs in the same frame — the watch is kept by one hand among empty chairs, not by an empty room. Prepro test: find the hand and the chairs — if either is missing, the watch is not yet staged. Sources: a lighthouse keeper's first night — the log witnesses the lone watch.
- **CRAFT-257 — A FIFTH LINK MUST BE SEALED, NOT COUNTED.** CHAIN-89 teaches that a fifth guest counted as a fifth link breaks the station's count, and a broken count ends the chain's trust. Rule: a draft staging a vouching beyond four links must show the book's seal across the chain's foot — the seal closes the chain the count cannot hold — before the fifth guest can be seated. Prepro test: find the seal — if the fifth line is counted, not sealed, the vouching is unclosed and the premise has not been staged yet. Sources: a web of trust — beyond depth, the seal carries trust, not the links.
- **CRAFT-258 — A FIRST WORD AFTER SILENCE MUST GREET, NOT MOVE.** CHAIN-90 teaches that a first word after silence that moves a motion is a fifth word, and a fifth word ends the three-word law the series built. Rule: a draft giving a silent worker a first word must make the word a greeting — of the hour, of the room, of the lamp — never a motion, a ruling, or a new hour. Prepro test: cover the motion — if the word still greets alone, it is a first word; if it moves something alone, it is a fifth word wearing a greeting. Sources: the talkies' first line — it greets before it moves.

### HS-63 — THE UNPRESSED SEAL (the sixth vouching refused)
When the inciting fact is a refused vouching (CHAIN-91's sixth guest), frame 0 must show the book's seal WHOLE and UNPRESSED beside a blank sixth line in the same frame — a pressed seal is a close; an absent seal is an unruled chain; an unpressed seal beside a written sixth name is a refusal. Restage rule: shoot the seal legible and unbroken beside the sixth name — if the seal is pressed, the chain is closed, not refused; if the seal is absent, the refusal has no mark. Companion to HS-62 (the fifth line): HS-62 makes a pressed seal a close; HS-63 makes an unpressed seal a refusal — one closes a chain, the other refuses a link. Sources: blackballing — one black ball excludes by ballot, not by voice (wikipedia.org "Blackballing").

### HS-64 — THE ENCORE WORD (the tender's second word)
When the inciting fact is a second word (CHAIN-92's tender mouth open a second time), frame 0 must show the mouth OPEN mid-second-word WITH the first greeting still logged uncrossed on the program sheet in the same frame — a second open mouth with the first greeting crossed is a motion; a second open mouth with the first greeting standing is an encore. Restage rule: shoot the sheet's uncrossed first greeting ("Heard again.") legible beside the chair — if the first greeting is crossed, the second word reads as a motion, not a repeat. Companion to HS-59 (the logged silence): HS-59 makes a closed mouth with a logged line a speech; HS-64 makes a second open mouth with an uncrossed greeting an encore — one writes a silence, the other repeats a greeting. Sources: the encore — an additional performance in response to applause, a repeat, not a new piece (wikipedia.org "Encore").

### LORE-32 — THE WITNESS BOOK (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-91 introduces the founder's witness law: "a refused guest is witnessed, not turned away." Backstory: the founder once refused a vouching and sent the guest from the door; the guest waited outside all night, and the station's log showed a night with a lamp but no witness — a kept watch no one could testify to; since then refused guests are entered in the witness book and seated in the gallery, so every night has a witness even when it has no seventh guest. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the witness book is the sixth guest's admission — CHAIN-91 P3's line: "Witnessed, not seated." Rule — the witness law: a refused guest is shown entered in the witness book and seated in the gallery, never at the table, never turned from the door — a refused guest turned away is a night unwitnessed. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26/LORE-27/LORE-28/LORE-29/LORE-30/LORE-31): set in CHAIN-91; the witness book is never opened before a refusal is ruled; a witness is never seated at the table — gallery only; the witness book's first reading never airs before CHAIN-94.

### CLIFF-MECH-31 — THE REFUSAL
The withheld fact is a LINK by a CLOSED BOOK — the cliff frame shows the book closed with the sixth name unwritten in the guest book (CHAIN-91 P1's unpressed seal beside a written sixth name), without saying whether the station refuses the guest or only the vouching. Rule: the vouching must be SHOWN written before it is refused — an unwritten vouching is no vouching; a written vouching beside an unpressed seal is a refusal. The next part spends it by RULING the guest witnessed (CHAIN-91 P3's log line: "SIXTH — WITNESSED, NOT SEATED.") — the spend is a ruling that keeps the person, not a transcript: the station names what the refusal kept, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-30 (the first word): the first word withholds a word by a return; the refusal withholds a link by a seal — one marks greeting, the other marks admission. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-27 (the overlap): the overlap withholds a watch by a handover; the refusal withholds a link by a seal — one marks duty, the other marks admission. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: blackballing — exclusion by ballot, one black ball (wikipedia.org "Blackballing").

- **CRAFT-259 — A REFUSAL MUST REFUSE THE VOUCHING, NOT THE GUEST.** CHAIN-91 teaches that a refusal that ejects the guest ends the hour's argument, and a refusal that keeps the guest as a witness extends it. Rule: a draft refusing a vouching must keep the refused person in frame — entered in the witness book, seated in the gallery — before the refusal can be ruled. Prepro test: find the witness — if the refused guest is gone from the frame, the refusal ejected a person, not a link, and the premise has not been staged yet. Sources: blackballing — the ballot excludes the candidate, but the club keeps its ballot box; the station keeps its witness.
- **CRAFT-260 — A SECOND WORD MUST ENCORE, NOT ADVANCE.** CHAIN-92 teaches that a second word that names anything new is a motion, and a motion ends the greeting law the series built. Rule: a draft giving a worker a second word must make the word a repeat of the first greeting — same hour, same lamp, nothing new named. Prepro test: cover the first greeting — if the second word still greets alone, it is an encore; if it names something the first greeting never named, it is a motion wearing a greeting. Sources: the encore — a repeat in response to applause, not a new piece.
- **CRAFT-261 — A RELIEF MUST KNOW THE PART BY WRITING IT.** CHAIN-93 teaches that a relief who arrives at the lamp without having written a watch is a stranger, and a stranger ends the transfer's argument. Rule: a draft sending a relief must show the relief at the log before the lamp — the relief's first frame is a writing hand, not a tending hand. Prepro test: find the writing frame — if the relief's first frame is at the lamp, the relief is unrehearsed; if the relief's first frame is at the log, the relief is an understudy. Sources: the understudy — a performer who learns the role by rehearsing it before stepping in.

### HS-65 — THE READ TESTIMONY (the witness book's first reading)

### CLIFF-MECH-32 — THE TESTIMONY
The withheld fact is an HOUR by a WITNESS — the cliff frame shows the witness book open with the witness's mouth CLOSED beside it (CHAIN-94 P1's called witness beside an open book), without saying whether the witness will speak the hour or keep it. Rule: the hour must be SHOWN watched before it is testified — an unwatched hour is no testimony; a watched hour beside a closed mouth is a testimony withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the witness speaks (CHAIN-94 P3's margin ruling: "TESTIMONY FIRSTHAND, HOUR NAMED.") — the spend is a ruling that keeps the hour, not a transcript: the station names what the testimony kept, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-31 (the refusal): the refusal withholds a link by a seal; the testimony withholds an hour by a witness — one marks admission, the other marks evidence. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-29 (the silence): the silence withholds a word by a seat; the testimony withholds an hour by a witness — one marks presence, the other marks evidence. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: a witness's testimony — evidence of what was seen, firsthand only (wikipedia.org "Witness", wikipedia.org "Hearsay").

Sources: watchkeeping — a resumed watch, not a stranger's watch.

### HS-67 — THE AMENDED TESTIMONY (the witness book's second reading)
When the inciting fact is a second reading (CHAIN-97's sixth guest), frame 0 must show the witness book OPEN in the gallery WITH one word CROSSED and no replacement written beside it yet, the witness standing beside it, mouth closed, in the same frame — a crossed word with a replacement already written is a ruling; a crossed word with no replacement is an amendment withheld; an uncrossed page is a first reading, not a second. Restage rule: shoot the crossed word legible beside the blank space where the replacement will go — if the word is uncrossed, the reading is a first, not a second; if the replacement is already written, the amendment is ruled, not withheld. Companion to HS-65 (the read testimony): HS-65 makes an open witness book beside a closed guest book a testimony; HS-67 makes a crossed word with no replacement an amendment — one speaks an hour, the other changes a word of it. Sources: a second reading — debate and amendment, not a repeat (wikipedia.org "Reading (legislature)").

### HS-68 — THE OVERTIME LAMP (the lamp kept past the hour)
When the inciting fact is a longer lamp (CHAIN-98's tender lamp), frame 0 must show the lamp LIT beside the log's hour line already CLOSED in the same frame — a lit lamp beside an open line is the hour; a dark lamp beside a closed line is the hour ended; a lit lamp beside a closed line is overtime. Restage rule: shoot the closed hour line legible beside the lit lamp — if the line is open, the lamp is inside its hour, not past it; if the lamp is dark, the overtime has no light to pay. Companion to HS-61 (the kept watch): HS-61 makes one hand among empty chairs a watch kept alone; HS-68 makes a lit lamp beside a closed line overtime — one keeps a watch, the other pays a lamp. Sources: overtime — time beyond the standard hour, counted as its own time (wikipedia.org "Overtime").

### LORE-34 — THE HOMECOMING LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-99 introduces the founder's homecoming law: "a keeper who returns twice is welcomed, not logged." Backstory: the founder once returned to his own station after a long absence and was logged as a visitor twice, because no rule welcomed a return — the log showed two visits and no homecoming, a keeper recorded as a stranger in his own station; since then a twice-returned keeper is welcomed with a line of their own in the log, and the welcome names the keeper, never the watch. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the homecoming law is the fifth hand's standing — CHAIN-99 P2's line: "Welcomed, kept." Rule — the homecoming law: a twice-returned keeper is shown welcomed with a line naming the keeper, never logged as a watch, never recorded as a visitor — a second return logged as a watch is a homecoming refused. ### CLIFF-MECH-33 — THE AMENDMENT
The withheld fact is a WORD by a CROSSING — the cliff frame shows the witness book open with one word crossed and the replacement unwritten (CHAIN-97 P1's struck word beside a blank space), without saying whether the amendment will keep the hour or change it. Rule: the word must be SHOWN struck before it is amended — an unstruck word is no amendment; a struck word beside a blank space is an amendment withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the amendment kept (CHAIN-97 P3's margin ruling: "AMENDED, HOUR KEPT.") — the spend is a ruling that keeps the text, not a transcript: the station names what the amendment kept, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-32 (the testimony): the testimony withholds an hour by a witness; the amendment withholds a word by a crossing — one marks evidence, the other marks revision. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-31 (the refusal): the refusal withholds a link by a seal; the amendment withholds a word by a crossing — one marks admission, the other marks revision. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: amendment — a formal change that keeps a text by changing a word in it (wikipedia.org "Amendment").

- **CRAFT-265 — A SECOND READING MUST AMEND, NOT REPEAT.** CHAIN-97 teaches that a second reading that respeaks the first testimony ends the amendment law the series built, and a second reading that changes one word extends it. Rule: a draft giving a witness a second reading must make the reading change exactly one word of the first testimony — the hour, the lamp, the night — never the whole text, never the guest. Prepro test: cover the first testimony — if the second reading still stands on its own, it is a repeat; if it collapses without the first text, it is an amendment. Sources: a second reading — debate and amendment, not a repeat.
- **CRAFT-266 — OVERTIME MUST BE A SECOND HOUR, NOT A LONGER ONE.** CHAIN-98 teaches that overtime logged as a longer first hour ends the counting law the series built, and overtime logged on its own line extends it. Rule: a draft keeping a lamp past the hour must give the overtime its own log line — a second hour, paid in writing — never a stretched first line. Prepro test: find the second line — if the overtime shares the first hour's line, it is a longer hour wearing overtime; if it has its own line, it is an hour added. Sources: overtime — counted as its own time.
- **CRAFT-267 — A HOMECOMING MUST WELCOME, NOT LOG.** CHAIN-99 teaches that a second return logged as a watch ends the homecoming law the series built, and a second return welcomed with its own line extends it. Rule: a draft returning a keeper a second time must write a welcome line naming the keeper — never a watch line, never a visitor line. Prepro test: find the welcome — if the log names the watch, the return was logged; if the log names the keeper, the return was welcomed. Sources: homecoming — marked by welcome, not by record alone.

The withheld fact is a KEEPER by a THIRD RETURN — the cliff frame shows the fifth hand at the receiving station door a third time with two welcome lines already written and a third line begun blank (CHAIN-102 P1's residence line begun: "RESIDENT —" with nothing after the dash), without saying whether the third return will be resided or welcomed again. Rule: the two welcomes must be SHOWN written before the third line is begun — a third line begun without two welcomes is no residence; two welcomes beside a begun third line is a residence withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the residence kept (CHAIN-102 P3's log ruling: "RESIDENCE KEPT BY THE FIFTH HAND, WRITTEN BY THE LOG-KEEPER.") — the spend is a ruling that keeps the dwelling, not a transcript: the station names what the residence kept, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-33 (the amendment): the amendment withholds a word by a crossing; the residence withholds a keeper by a third return — one marks revision, the other marks dwelling. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-32 (the testimony): the testimony withholds an hour by a witness; the residence withholds a keeper by a return — one marks evidence, the other marks dwelling. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: residence — one who dwells in a place as their own, not one who visits it (wikipedia.org "Residence").

- **CRAFT-268 — A THIRD READING MUST PASS, NOT AMEND AGAIN.** CHAIN-100 teaches that a third reading that re-amends the testimony ends the passage law the series built, and a third reading that votes the amended text extends it. Rule: a draft giving a witness a third reading must make the reading put the amended testimony to the station's vote — passage or no passage — never a second amendment, never a respoken first text. Prepro test: cover the amendment — if the third reading still stands on its own, it is a new text, not a passage; if it collapses without the amended text, it is a passage. Sources: a third reading — final passage stage, not a debate again.
- **CRAFT-269 — SECOND OVERTIME MUST BE DOUBLE, NOT LONGER STILL.** CHAIN-101 teaches that a second overtime logged as a longer first overtime ends the counting law the series built, and a second overtime logged on its own second line extends it. Rule: a draft keeping a lamp past a second hour must give the second overtime its own second log line — a second overtime, paid in writing — never a stretched first overtime line. Prepro test: find the second line — if the second overtime shares the first overtime's line, it is a longer overtime wearing a second; if it has its own line, it is an overtime added. Sources: double time — counted as its own premium time.
- **CRAFT-270 — A THIRD RETURN MUST RESIDE, NOT WELCOME AGAIN.** CHAIN-102 teaches that a third return welcomed with a third welcome line ends the residence law the series built, and a third return resided with its own residence line extends it. Rule: a draft returning a keeper a third time must write a residence line naming the keeper — never a third welcome line, never a visitor line. Sources: residence — marked by dwelling, not by welcome alone.

### HS-73 — THE PROMULGATED RECORD (the record book's fifth reading)
When the inciting fact is a fifth reading (CHAIN-106's sixth guest), frame 0 must show the record book OPEN in the gallery WITH the confirmation line legible AND the station's seal PRESSED on the confirmation line, the witness standing beside it, mouth closed, in the same frame — a raised seal above a confirmation line is a passage awaiting a vote; a pressed seal on an unconfirmed line is a passage, not a promulgation; a pressed seal on the confirmation line beside an open record book is a promulgation. Restage rule: shoot the pressed seal legible on the confirmation line beside the open record book — if the seal is raised, the record is voted, not promulgated; if the record book is closed, the reading is a testimony, not a promulgation. Companion to HS-71 (the confirmed record): HS-71 makes a blank confirmation line beside an open record book a confirmation; HS-73 makes a pressed seal on the confirmation line a promulgation — one confirms the record, the other publishes it. Sources: promulgation — a law is published so that it takes effect (wikipedia.org "Promulgation").

### HS-74 — THE RELIEVED LAMP (the lamp kept past the fourth hour)
When the inciting fact is a fourth overtime (CHAIN-107's tender lamp), frame 0 must show the lamp LIT beside the log's shift line already CLOSED and a relief line BEGUN in a NEW hand beneath it in the same frame — a lit lamp beside an open shift line is the shift; a dark lamp beside a closed shift line is the shift ended; a lit lamp beside a closed shift line with a relief line begun in a new hand is a relief. Restage rule: shoot the closed shift line and the begun relief line legible beside the lit lamp, the relief line in a hand distinct from the shift line's — if the shift line is open, the lamp is inside its shift, not past it; if the relief line shares the shift's hand, the fourth overtime has no relief, only a longer shift. Companion to HS-72 (the shifted lamp): HS-72 makes a lit lamp beside a closed second overtime line with a shift line begun a shift; HS-74 makes a lit lamp beside a closed shift line with a relief line begun a relief — one hands the lamp to a new tender, the other hands it to a new hand. ### LORE-37 — THE SETTLEMENT LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-108 introduces the founder's settlement law: "a keeper who returns a fifth time stays." Backstory: the founder once wrote a coverage for every return of a resident who kept returning, because no rule settled a keeper — the log showed coverage upon coverage for a keeper who had never departed, a resident recorded as if each staying were a new arrival; since then a fifth return settles the residence, and the log closes the residence line as settled, never adding another coverage. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the settlement law is the fifth hand's standing — CHAIN-108 P2's line: "Stays, settled." Rule — the settlement law: a fifth return is shown settled by a closed settlement line, never given another coverage, never recorded as a return — a fifth return given a new coverage is a settlement refused. ### CLIFF-MECH-36 — THE SETTLEMENT
The withheld fact is a STAY by a CLOSED LINE — the cliff frame shows the fifth hand at the receiving station door a fifth time with the residence line open and the coverage mark already beside it and the space beneath it blank (CHAIN-108 P1's open residence line with coverage already marked, nothing settled beneath it), without saying whether the fifth return will be covered again or settled. Rule: the residence line must be SHOWN covered before the fifth return is settled — an uncovered residence line is no settlement; a covered residence line beside a blank space beneath it is a settlement withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the settlement kept (CHAIN-108 P3's log ruling: "RESIDENCE SETTLED — FIFTH RETURN STAYS, NO DEPARTURE.") — the spend is a ruling that keeps the keeper, not a transcript: the station names what the settlement kept, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-35 (the coverage): the coverage withholds a return by an open line; the settlement withholds a stay by a closed line — one marks coverage, the other marks settlement. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-34 (the residence): the residence withholds a keeper by a third return; the settlement withholds a stay by a fifth return — one marks dwelling, the other marks staying. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: settlement — a settler dwells in a place as their own (wikipedia.org "Settler").

- **CRAFT-274 — A FIFTH READING MUST PROMULGATE, NOT CONFIRM AGAIN.** CHAIN-106 teaches that a fifth reading that re-confirms the record ends the promulgation law the series built, and a fifth reading that reads the confirmed record aloud extends it. Rule: a draft giving a record a fifth reading must make the reading promulgate the record as confirmed — read aloud, binding — never a second confirmation, never a re-amendment. Prepro test: cover the confirmation — if the fifth reading still stands on its own, it is a new confirmation, not a promulgation; if it collapses without the confirmed record, it is a promulgation. Sources: promulgation — publication gives a law effect, not a second vote.
- **CRAFT-275 — A FOURTH OVERTIME MUST RELIEVE, NOT SHIFT AGAIN.** CHAIN-107 teaches that a fourth overtime logged as a longer shift ends the relief law the series built, and a fourth overtime logged on a relief line extends it. Rule: a draft keeping a lamp past a fourth hour must give the fourth overtime a relief line in a new hand — a relief begun — never a stretched shift line. Prepro test: find the new hand — if the fourth overtime shares the shift's tender, it is a longer shift wearing a relief; if it has its own hand, it is a relief begun. Sources: relief — the next hand, with its own line.
- **CRAFT-276 — A FIFTH RETURN MUST SETTLE, NOT COVER AGAIN.** CHAIN-108 teaches that a fifth return given a new coverage ends the settlement law the series built, and a fifth return closed as settled extends it. Rule: a draft returning a resident a fifth time must close the residence line as settled and write no new coverage beneath it — never a fifth coverage line, never a fifth welcome line, never a return line. Prepro test: find the new coverage — if the log adds one beneath the residence line, the return was covered; if the residence line closes as settled and alone, the return was settled. Sources: settlement — marked by a line closed, not by a line added.

### HS-79 — THE DISTINGUISHED RECORD (the record book's first distinction)
When the inciting fact is a first distinction (CHAIN-115's eighth guest), frame 0 must show the record book OPEN in the gallery WITH the precedent line legible AND CLOSED and a distinction line BEGUN beneath it naming the differing material fact, the witness standing beside it, mouth closed, in the same frame — an open precedent line beside a begun distinction is a precedent, not a distinction; a closed precedent line with no distinction begun is a record followed, not distinguished; a closed precedent line with a distinction begun beneath it naming the fact is a distinction. Restage rule: shoot the closed precedent line and the begun distinction line legible beside the open record book — if the precedent line is open, the record is still being followed, not distinguished; if no distinction line is begun, the record is followed, not distinguished. Companion to HS-77 (the followed record): HS-77 makes a begun precedent beneath a closed citation line a precedent; HS-79 makes a begun distinction beneath a closed precedent line a distinction — one follows the cited record, the other distinguishes the followed record. Sources: distinguishing is "the main device for avoiding binding precedent... distinguishing the previous case as having different material facts" (open.edu OpenLearn "Legal skills and debates in Scotland: 2.3.2 Distinguishing").

### HS-80 — THE DAYLIGHT LAMP (the lamp burning in daylight)
When the inciting fact is a first daylight (CHAIN-116's day hand), frame 0 must show the lamp LIT in daylight beside the log's dawn line already CLOSED and a day line BEGUN in the DAY hand beneath it in the same frame — a lit lamp beside an open dawn line is a dawn unfinished; a dark lamp beside a closed dawn line is a lamp out; a lit lamp in daylight beside a closed dawn line with a day line begun in the day hand is daylight. Restage rule: shoot the closed dawn line and the begun day line legible beside the lit lamp in daylight, the day line in the day hand — if the dawn line is open, the lamp is still being returned, not burned; if no day line is begun, the lamp is returned, not burned. Companion to HS-78 (the returned lamp): HS-78 makes a lit lamp beside a closed watch line with a dawn line begun a dawn; HS-80 makes a lit lamp in daylight beside a closed dawn line with a day line begun a daylight — one returns the lamp at first light, the other burns it through the forenoon. Sources: the forenoon watch, 8am to noon, after the morning watch 4am to 8am (h2g2.com "Bell Time").

### LORE-40 — THE DISTINCTION LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-115 introduces the founder's distinction law: "a record distinguished binds the distinction, not the record." Backstory: the founder once watched a following applied to a case that differed in one material fact, because no rule bound a distinction — the log showed following upon following for a case already distinguished, a case followed as if the differing fact were no fact at all; since then a distinction binds the distinction, and the record itself is never re-followed on the differing fact. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the distinction law is the eighth guest's standing — CHAIN-115 P2's line: "As followed." Rule — the distinction law: a first distinction is shown distinguishing by a closed distinction line beneath a closed precedent line, never by a new precedent, never by a re-following — a distinction given a new precedent is a following refused. Placement law (shared with LORE-19/LORE-20/LORE-21/LORE-22/LORE-23/LORE-24/LORE-25/LORE-26/LORE-27/LORE-28/LORE-29/LORE-30/LORE-31/LORE-32/LORE-33/LORE-34/LORE-35/LORE-36/LORE-37/LORE-38/LORE-39): set in CHAIN-115; the distinction line never airs before CHAIN-115; a record is never distinguished before followed; the distinction's first application never airs before CHAIN-118.

### CLIFF-MECH-39 — THE DISTINCTION
The withheld fact is a DISTINCTION by a BEGUN LINE — the cliff frame shows the record book open with the precedent line closed and a distinction line begun beneath it naming the differing fact and the space beneath it blank (CHAIN-115 P1's closed precedent line with distinction begun, nothing ruled beneath it), without saying whether the distinction follows the precedent or breaks it. Rule: the precedent line must be SHOWN closed before a distinction follows — an open precedent line is no distinction; a closed precedent line beside a begun distinction line is a distinction withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the distinction kept (CHAIN-115 P3's log ruling: "DISTINGUISHED, BINDING.") — the spend is a ruling that follows the precedent on the differing fact, not a transcript: the station names what the distinction followed, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-38 (the precedent): the precedent withholds a following by a begun line; the distinction withholds a distinction by a begun line — one follows a cited record, the other distinguishes a followed record. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-37 (the citation): the citation withholds a binding by a begun line; the distinction withholds a distinction by a begun line — one binds a citing line, the other distinguishes a followed record. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: distinguishing — a previous case distinguished as having different material facts (open.edu OpenLearn "Legal skills and debates in Scotland: 2.3.2 Distinguishing").

- **CRAFT-283 — A FIRST DISTINCTION MUST FOLLOW, NOT BREAK.** CHAIN-115 teaches that a first distinction that breaks the precedent ends the distinction law the series built, and a first distinction that follows the precedent on the differing fact extends it. Rule: a draft distinguishing a record must make the distinction follow the precedent on the fact that differs — followed, closed — never a new precedent, never a re-following. Prepro test: cover the differing fact — if the distinction still stands on its own, it is a new precedent, not a distinction; if it collapses without the differing fact, it is a distinction. Sources: distinguishing — a case distinguished on different material facts, not a republication.
- **CRAFT-284 — A FIRST DAYLIGHT MUST BURN, NOT WATCH AGAIN.** CHAIN-116 teaches that a first daylight logged as a second watch ends the daylight law the series built, and a first daylight logged as a burning extends it. Rule: a draft burning a lamp in daylight must give the daylight a forenoon line — a burning begun — never a second watch, never the same watch past eight bells. Prepro test: find the forenoon line — if the daylight shares the watch's line, it is a longer watch wearing daylight; if it has its own forenoon line, it is a burning begun. Sources: forenoon watch — 8am to noon, after the morning watch 4am to 8am, ending at eight bells.
- **CRAFT-285 — A FIRST DAY LIVED MUST KEEP, NOT ARRIVE AGAIN.** CHAIN-117 teaches that a first day lived written as an arrival ends the day law the series built, and a first day lived kept as a keeping extends it. Rule: a draft living a keeper's day must close the day line as kept with no arrival beneath it — never a welcome line, never an arrival line, never a return line. Prepro test: find the arrival — if the log adds one beneath the day line, the day was an arrival; if the day line closes as kept and alone, the day was lived. Sources: dayworkers — a standard day lived by its hours, not by watches.

### LORE-41 — THE APPLICATION LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-118 introduces the founder's application law: "a distinction applied binds the application, not the distinction." Backstory: the founder once watched a distinction re-distinguished on every new case, because no rule bound an application — the log showed distinction upon distinction for a case already applied, a case distinguished as if the application were no application at all; since then an application binds the application, and the distinction itself is never re-distinguished on the similar case. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the application law is the ninth guest's standing — CHAIN-118 P2's line: "On all fours." Rule — the application law: a first application is shown applying by a closed application line beneath a closed distinction line, never by a new distinction, never by a re-distinction — an application given a new distinction is an application refused. ### CLIFF-MECH-40 — THE APPLICATION
The withheld fact is an APPLICATION by a BEGUN LINE — the cliff frame shows the record book open with the distinction line closed and an application line begun beneath it naming the case on all fours and the space beneath it blank (CHAIN-118 P1's closed distinction line with application begun, nothing ruled beneath it), without saying whether the application applies the distinction or re-distinguishes it. Rule: the distinction line must be SHOWN closed before an application follows — an open distinction line is no application; a closed distinction line beside a begun application line is an application withheld. The next part spends it by RULING the application kept (CHAIN-118 P3's log ruling: "APPLIED, BINDING.") — the spend is a ruling that applies the distinction on the differing fact, not a transcript: the station names what the application applied, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-39 (the distinction): the distinction withholds a distinction by a begun line; the application withholds an application by a begun line — one distinguishes a followed record, the other applies a distinguished record. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). - **CRAFT-286 — A FIRST APPLICATION MUST APPLY, NOT RE-DISTINGUISH.** CHAIN-118 teaches that a first application that re-distinguishes the record ends the application law the series built, and a first application that applies the distinction on the differing fact extends it. - **CRAFT-287 — A FIRST NOON MUST BURN ON, NOT RELIGHT.** CHAIN-119 teaches that a first noon logged as a relighting ends the noon law the series built, and a first noon logged as a burning-on extends it. Prepro test: find the relighting — if the noon shares the daylight's line, it is a longer daylight wearing noon; if it has its own afternoon line, it is a noon begun. Sources: afternoon watch — noon to 4pm, after the forenoon watch 8am to noon, eight bells at noon.
- **CRAFT-288 — A FIRST EVENING MUST KEEP, NOT NIGHT AGAIN.** CHAIN-120 teaches that a first evening written as a new night ends the evening law the series built, and a first evening kept as a keeping extends it. Rule: a draft eveninging a keeper must close the evening line as kept with no new night beneath it — never a night line, never a middle-watch line, never a second first night. Prepro test: find the new night — if the log adds one beneath the evening line, the evening was a night; if the evening line closes as kept and alone, the evening was lived. Sources: first watch — 8pm to midnight, after the dog watches 4pm to 8pm, split so no crew stands the middle of every night.

### HS-85 — THE SETTLED RETURN (the record book's first settlement)
When the inciting fact is a first settlement (CHAIN-124's settler), frame 0 must show the record book OPEN in the gallery WITH the following line legible AND CLOSED and a settlement line BEGUN beneath it in a hand with no guest line anywhere in the book, the settler standing beside it, mouth closed, in the same frame — a closed following line beside a begun settlement in a held hand is a guest settling, not a return; an open following line beside a begun settlement is a following unsettled, not settled; a closed following line with a settlement begun in an unheld hand is a return. Restage rule: shoot the closed following line and the begun settlement line legible beside the open record book, the settling hand visibly unheld — if the hand matches a guest line, the settlement is a guest's, not a return; if no settlement line is begun, the record is followed, not settled. Companion to HS-83 (the followed application): HS-83 makes a begun following beneath a closed application line a following; HS-85 makes a begun settlement in an unheld hand beneath a closed following line a return — one follows the applied record, the other returns to settle the followed record. Sources: the return as revelation and dramatic irony — the audience learning the hand is unheld before the characters do (tvtropes.org "SoapOpera"); drop the revelation, then stop (serial.ca "The Psychology Behind Cliffhangers").

### HS-86 — THE COUNTED LINE (the counting board's eleventh tally — Super Number Head planted)
When the inciting fact is a first count (CHAIN-124's bridge: the settlement's first count), frame 0 must show the counting board beside the log WITH eleven tallies on the board AND ten guest lines in the log, Super Number Head — the station's numbers-obsessed head-of-counting figure, original WuBu-native character — standing beside the board, mouth closed, in the same frame — eleven tallies beside eleven lines is a ledger, not a count; ten tallies beside ten lines is a ledger kept, not a count; eleven tallies beside ten lines with the head-of-counting beside them is a count. Restage rule: shoot the board's eleventh tally and the log's ten lines legible in one frame, the head-of-counting beside the board — if the tallies match the lines, there is nothing to count; if no eleventh tally stands, the count is a recount, not a first count. Companion to HS-85 (the settled return): HS-85 makes an unheld hand settling a return; HS-86 makes an uncounted tally counting a return — one settles the eleventh guest, the other counts them. Placement law: Super Number Head's first count never airs before the chain that spends CHAIN-124's bridge; the head-of-counting never counts before the settlement settles.

### LORE-43 — THE SETTLEMENT LAW (station history as serial setting)
CHAIN-124 introduces the founder's settlement law: "a settlement settles the following, not the guest." Backstory: the founder once watched a following re-settled on every new guest, because no rule bound a settlement — the log showed settlement upon settlement for a following already settled, a following settled as if the settlement were no settlement at all; since then a settlement binds the settlement, and the following itself is never re-settled on the settled case. Cast backstory that pays off in a line: the settlement law is the eleventh guest's standing — CHAIN-124 P2's line: "As followed." Rule — the settlement law: a first settlement is shown settling by a closed settlement line beneath a closed following line, never by a new following, never by a re-settlement — a settlement given a new following is a settlement refused. Placement law (shared with LORE-19 through LORE-42): set in CHAIN-124; the settlement line never airs before CHAIN-124; a following is never settled before followed; the settlement's first count never airs before the chain that spends CHAIN-124's bridge.

### CLIFF-MECH-42 — THE SETTLEMENT
The withheld fact is a SETTLEMENT by a BEGUN LINE — the cliff frame shows the record book open with the following line closed and a settlement line begun beneath it in an unheld hand and the space beneath it blank (CHAIN-124 P1's closed following line with settlement begun, nothing ruled beneath it), without saying whose hand settles. The next part spends it by RULING the settlement kept (CHAIN-124 P3's log ruling: "SETTLED, ELEVENTH GUEST.") — the spend is a ruling that settles the following on the followed fact, not a transcript: the station names what the settlement settled, never quotes it. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-41 (the following): the following withholds a following by a begun line; the settlement withholds a settlement by a begun line — one follows an applied record, the other settles a followed record. Companion to CLIFF-MECH-40 (the application): the application withholds an application by a begun line; the settlement withholds a settlement by a begun line — one applies a distinguished record, the other settles a followed record. The three never co-occur in one chain (CRAFT-202's one-trigger rule audits this). Sources: settlement — drop the revelation, then stop (serial.ca "The Psychology Behind Cliffhangers").

- **CRAFT-292 — A GRABBING HOOK MUST ASK, NOT TELL.** CHAIN-124 teaches that a first settlement framed as an explanation ("a stranger settles") ends the hook the series built, and a first settlement framed as a question (an unheld hand, a begun line, nothing ruled) extends it. - **CRAFT-294 — AN IRONIC PAYOFF MUST COST THE PROVER.** CHAIN-126 teaches that an ironic payoff the keeper watches from outside ends the irony the series built, and an ironic payoff the keeper earns by standing extends it. Rule: a draft paying off a pre-written standing must make the keeper stand the watch — the proof must be the standing itself — never a bystander reading the payoff aloud. Prepro test: remove the keeper's standing — if the payoff still lands, it is a twist observed, not irony earned; if it collapses without the standing, it is irony. Sources: the ironic shape — ordinary situation plus uncanny turn plus a payoff revealing the character's true relationship to the situation; the answer-new-mystery equilibrium — a cliffhanger answers exactly enough to satisfy while presenting a new riddle (soapcentral.com "Severance creators reveal the secret to a great cliffhanger").
